A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BRIDGE research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. Changes and inconsistencies in reported experimental settings can be identified without preventing comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original mathematical-reasoning evaluations, training dynamics, efficiency measurements, OOD results, and LoRA sensitivity experiments, including appendix material.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds hybrid-baseline comparisons, logical-reasoning experiments, ablations, reward-noise tests, and appendix sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: BRIDGE retains its bilevel objective, base-model/LoRA separation, mixed student gradients, RL-only auxiliary iterate, and cooperative-gain teacher update (v2 Algorithm 2; v3 Algorithm 1). Shared-rollout scoring and LoRA merging are newly documented implementation details. Removing the annealing discussion does not establish a procedural change because v2 Appendix B already specifies fixed lambda=0.5.

E1.justification: v3 adds training and evaluation on Knights-and-Knaves logical reasoning, including unseen configurations with 6–8 players, and mathematics experiments with deliberately corrupted rewards. These substantially extend domain and test-scenario coverage. The five mathematics benchmarks and code/science OOD evaluations already occur in v2.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 add evaluated LUFFY, SRFT, and CHORD baselines. The sequential Naive Alternating comparator is removed; v3's joint-loss SFT+RL is a different procedure. RL-zero/RL and Cold-start/SFT→RL are renamings. Appendix A adds periodic SFT-refresh controls, and the OOD comparison replaces the Instruct row with SFT.

E3.justification: For Qwen2.5-3B, reported training data changes from 1.3k LIMR examples to the 8.5k MATH hard split. Batch size changes from 64 to 128, 3B rollouts from 5 to 8, and response caps from 3k/8k to 4k for Qwen2.5 and 6k for Llama/Qwen3. New protocols include Pass@4/8/16/32 and reward flipping. The OOD backbone changes from Qwen3-8B to Qwen2.5-3B despite identical retained scores. These are reported setting changes; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of the meta-objective's necessity, periodic supervision, mixing-weight sensitivity, solution coverage through Pass@K, reward-noise robustness, and harder logical configurations. The epoch-by-epoch analysis in v2 Table 5 and Appendix C is removed. The existing LoRA sensitivity experiment is retained as v3 Table 11 and Appendix A.2, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard errors, or significance tests. LoRA configuration variability and the newly described shared-rollout scoring do not introduce uncertainty reporting for the experimental results.

E6.justification: v3 adds hybrid-baseline, logic, meta-ablation, Pass@K, noise, refresh, and mixing-weight results while removing alternating and epoch-sweep entries. Table 5 newly reports 49.9 with versus 40.3 without the meta-objective. Main BRIDGE averages remain 36.0/24.7/49.9, but the cost table's 3B accuracy changes from 36.4 to 36.0. SFT AIME24/AMC23 entries change from 27.5/3.3 to 3.3/27.5 for Llama and 45.0/13.3 to 13.3/45.0 for Qwen3. Reported setting changes preclude interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 adds an asserted O(1−lambda) distance bound for penalty solutions in Section 3.2 and derives how binary reward flipping rescales the expected cooperative gain by 1−2p in Equation 11. The underlying bilevel formulation and first-order update derivation remain intact; these are limited formal additions.

C1.justification: The central argument shifts from catastrophic forgetting in two-stage training toward potentially harmful supervision in hybrid training. v3 drops the alternating-baseline contribution and unqualified performance-guarantee language, while adding claims about superiority over recent hybrids, logical reasoning, preserved solution diversity, and robustness to noisy rewards.

C2.justification: v3 removes the explicit interpretation of response-length decline as catastrophic forgetting. It adds explanations involving the LoRA teacher reshaping the optimization landscape, expert traces enriching exploration, and noise cancellation in cooperative gain. New limitations exclude open-ended subjective rewards and discuss auxiliary-model memory at untested 70B+ scales.

D1.justification: v3 substantially revises the reproducibility description: it specifies GRPO, KL/entropy coefficients, two training epochs, the teacher learning rate, shared-rollout scoring, and merged-LoRA inference. It also supplies a promised code-release URL, without establishing availability. Conversely, v2's explicit DeepMath-103k trace-source identification, SimpleRL prompt-format statement, LiveCodeBench v5 designation, default LoRA configuration, and separate evaluation token limits are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around objective-level integration and data-augmented RL, adding SRFT, interleaved and adaptive integration studies, and exploration literature. CHORD and LUFFY were already discussed in v2, but their relationship to BRIDGE is developed within a broader taxonomy. LIMR and PPO citations disappear; the existing bilevel-literature discussion is largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminary analysis, method explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around learning useful supervision. Analysis and generalization receive dedicated sections; implementation details and extended related work move into the main text. Appendices are reorganized, limitations and disclosure sections are added, and the earlier LLM-writing disclosure is removed.

P2.justification: The main document changes from single-column to two-column layout. The conceptual diagram expands from two training methods to three paradigms. Training dynamics are redrawn as metric-specific panels with an additional comparator, rather than separate method panels. Main tables are expanded and regrouped, multiple analysis tables are added, and the epoch table is removed; the LoRA table is retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the empirical case through evaluated hybrid baselines, the meta-objective ablation, stress tests, and explicit limitations. However, it removes the competitive alternating baseline and retains most scores despite revised settings. The OOD table changes its stated backbone without explanation (v2 Table 4; v3 Table 7). The introduction also claims logical transfer without additional training, whereas Section 6 reports logic training. These unresolved attribution and claim-evidence inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the useful additions.
